title: Lexicographically Smallest String After Reverse II
summary: Given a string s, you can reverse either the first k characters or the last k characters for any k from 1 to n.
statement: Given a string s, you can reverse either the first k characters or the last k characters for any k from 1 to n. Perform exactly one such operation to achieve the lexicographically smallest possible string.
constraints: s contains one to 100,000 lowercase letters.
Perform exactly one prefix reversal or suffix reversal of any length.
Return the lexicographically smallest obtainable string.
hints: Each candidate is a concatenation of at most two substrings from s and its reversal.
Represent candidates by those segments and compare them with binary-searched longest common prefixes from double rolling hashes.
Inspect every prefix and suffix length, retaining only candidates whose first character can match the global minimum.
The segment representation exactly describes each legal reversal, while hash-based LCP comparison orders two candidates without constructing them.
editorial: The segment representation exactly describes each legal reversal, while hash-based LCP comparison orders two candidates without constructing them.

tests.explanation: Reversing the first three letters produces acdb, the smallest result.
Reversing the final three letters produces aabb.
